label: Acts 21:1
text: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 21:1 Παταρα for א, B and most witnesses - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, Πατερα is listed for P74, A and C, and Παταρα και Μυρα ('Patara and Myra') for P41 and D. The WEB prints the 'Patara' wording.

label: Acts 21:2
text: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.

label: Acts 21:3
text: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

label: Acts 21:4
text: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

label: Acts 21:5
text: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.

label: Acts 21:8
text:
On the next day, we, who were Paul’s companions, departed, and came to Caesarea.
We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

label: Acts 21:10
text: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

label: Acts 21:11
text: Coming to us, and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “Thus says the Holy Spirit: ‘So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”

label: Acts 21:12
text: When we heard these things, both we and they of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

label: Acts 21:13
text: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

label: Acts 21:14
text: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”

label: Acts 21:15

text: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.

label: Acts 21:22
text: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.

label: Acts 21:23

label: Acts 21:24
text: Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.

text: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”

label: Acts 21:26

label: Paul's party sailed with a straight course to Cos, then Rhodes, then Patara
statement: After leaving the Ephesian elders, Paul's company sailed a straight course to Cos, the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

label: They found a ship crossing to Phoenicia and went aboard
statement: At Patara they found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, went aboard, and set sail.

label: They sighted Cyprus on the left and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload
statement: Coming in sight of Cyprus and leaving it on the left hand, they sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload her cargo.

label: Disciples at Tyre hosted Paul seven days and through the Spirit urged him not to go to Jerusalem
statement: Having found disciples at Tyre, Paul's party stayed there seven days; through the Spirit the disciples said Paul should not go up to Jerusalem.
note: A Spirit-given warning is a prediction; evidence could at most attest the seven-day stay, never the Spirit's utterance.

label: The Tyrian disciples with wives and children escorted them to the beach, knelt and prayed
statement: When the days were over, all the Tyrian disciples, with wives and children, brought them out of the city; kneeling on the beach they prayed, said goodbye and Paul's party went aboard.

label: They reached Ptolemais, greeted the brothers and stayed one day
statement: Finishing the voyage from Tyre, they arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

label: They came to Caesarea and stayed at the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven
statement: The next day they came to Caesarea and entered the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven, and stayed with him.

label: Philip had four virgin daughters who prophesied
statement: Philip the evangelist had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
note: A prediction/gift claim: evidence could at most attest Philip's family tradition, never that the daughters prophesied. Reception in Eusebius 3.39.9 (Papias) is graded D.

label: The prophet Agabus came down from Judea to Caesarea
statement: As they stayed some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

label: Agabus bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt and predicted the Jews would bind its owner
statement: Agabus took Paul's belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, 'Thus says the Holy Spirit: So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man who owns this belt, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'
note: A prediction: evidence can at most attest that the predicted arrest came to pass, never the prediction or its Spirit-source. The event is narrated in Acts 22-24; no external record.

label: Companions and Caesarean believers begged Paul not to go; he answered he was ready to die; they said 'the Lord's will be done'
statement: Hearing Agabus's warning, Paul's companions and the believers of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem; Paul answered he was ready not only to be bound but to die at Jerusalem, and they ceased, saying, 'The Lord's will be done.'

label: They went up to Jerusalem with Caesarean disciples bringing Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple
statement: After these days Paul's party took up their baggage and went up to Jerusalem; some disciples from Caesarea came with them, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom they would stay.

label: The Jerusalem brothers received Paul and his companions gladly
statement: When they came to Jerusalem, the brothers received them gladly.

label: Paul went in with the party to James, and all the elders were present
statement: The next day Paul went in with the others to James, and all the elders were present.
note: No external source records this meeting. Josephus, Ant. 20.200, independently attests James the brother of Jesus as a leading Jerusalem figure in the early 60s (grade A on the person).

label: Paul reported one by one the things God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry
statement: Paul greeted the elders and related one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.

label: The elders said many thousands of Jews believed and were all zealous for the law
statement: The elders glorified God and told Paul: 'You see, brother, how many thousands (myriades) there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.'

label: The elders said the believers had been informed that Paul taught Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses
statement: The elders said Paul had been informed about: that he teaches all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to walk after the customs.

label: Four men were under a vow; Paul was asked to purify himself with them and pay their expenses so they could shave their heads
statement: James and the elders proposed: 'We have four men who have taken a vow. Take them, and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses, that they may shave their heads' - so all would know Paul walked keeping the law. The vow is traditionally understood as the nazirite vow (Numbers 6).
note: Evidence confirms the vow practice (Mishnah Nazir, redacted c. 200 CE, may not describe the practice of the 30s CE exactly) and a Herodian-era precedent of a patron covering nazirite costs (Josephus, Ant. 19.294).

label: The elders repeated the written decision that believing Gentiles abstain from idol food, blood, strangled things and sexual immorality
statement: The elders said that concerning the Gentiles who believe, they had written their decision: they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.
note: The same four abstentions as Acts 15:20, 29; the two narrative statements are related, not independent evidence for each other.

label: Paul purified himself with the four men, went into the temple, and announced the completion of the days of purification until the offering for each
statement: Paul took the men, and the next day, purified himself with them and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

label: Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple, stirred up the multitude and laid hands on him
statement: When the seven days were almost completed, Jews from Asia, seeing Paul in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him.

label: The Asian Jews cried out that Paul taught against the people, the law and this place, and had brought Greeks into the temple
statement: The Jews from Asia cried out, 'Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple, and has defiled this holy place!'
note: No external record of this charge; the Temple warning inscription attests the exclusion rule that made a Greek in the inner courts the defiling act the charge presupposes (see the separate custom claim).

label: Gentiles were forbidden past the Temple balustrade into the inner courts on pain of death
statement: In the Jerusalem temple of this period, Gentiles (non-Jews) were excluded from the inner courts beyond the balustrade (soreg) on pain of death - the exclusion that gave the charge 'he brought Greeks into the temple' its force.

label: The Asian Jews had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city and supposed Paul brought him into the temple
statement: The accusers had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city, and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

label: The whole city was moved; Paul was dragged out of the temple and the doors were shut
statement: All the city was moved, the people ran together, seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple; immediately the doors were shut.

label: A Roman tribune (chiliarch) commanding a cohort was stationed in Jerusalem adjacent to the temple
statement: News of the uproar came up to the commanding officer of the regiment (chiliarchos), showing that a Roman military tribune with troops was stationed in Jerusalem right at the temple complex.

label: The tribune took soldiers and centurions and ran down; the crowd stopped beating Paul
statement: The tribune immediately took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them; when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

label: The tribune arrested Paul, bound him with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done
statement: The commanding officer came near, arrested Paul, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.

label: Paul was taken into the barracks (parembole), a military post adjoining the temple reached by stairs from the temple courts
statement: Unable to learn the truth in the uproar, the tribune had Paul brought into the barracks (parembole); on the stairs the soldiers carried Paul because of the crowd's violence, and the multitude followed crying 'Away with him!'
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Paul asked the tribune in Greek for permission to speak, and the tribune replied 'Do you know Greek?'
statement: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks he asked the tribune, 'May I speak to you?' The tribune answered, 'Do you know Greek?'

label: The tribune asked whether Paul was the Egyptian who stirred up sedition and led 4,000 sicarii into the wilderness
statement: The tribune asked: 'Aren't you then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?' - recalling a recent revolt of an Egyptian prophet.
note: Josephus independently attests the Egyptian and his revolt (A), but says thirty thousand followers, against Acts' four thousand sicarii (recorded as complicates).

label: The 'Assassins' (sicarii) were dagger-men active in Jerusalem in this period
statement: The 'men of the Assassins' the tribune names are the Sicarii, the dagger-wielding group active in Jerusalem around this period.

label: Tarsus in Cilicia was a city of consequence - 'no insignificant city'
statement: Paul answered, 'I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city' - Tarsus was the metropolis of Cilicia, celebrated for learning.
note: Evidence attests the city's standing, not that Paul said this or that he was its citizen (a claim of Acts).

label: Paul stood on the stairs, motioned for silence, and addressed the crowd in the Hebrew language
statement: The tribune gave permission; Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand, and when there was a great silence he spoke to them in the Hebrew language (Hebrais, commonly understood as Aramaic).

title: The War of the Jews - Book II
excerpt: But there was an Egyptian false prophet that did the Jews more mischief than the former; for he was a cheat, and pretended to be a prophet also, and got together thirty thousand men

label: An Egyptian false prophet led a seditious crowd to the Mount of Olives under Felix
statement: An Egyptian false prophet stirred up sedition, led a large crowd of people out of the wilderness toward the Mount of Olives in the days of Felix, and Felix attacked the crowd with cavalry.
note: Event claim split from claim:ac-21-38-egyptian-4000 (architect's Acts 21 log: split out the Egyptian's rising as an A claim); the Acts 21:38 rumour claim keeps grade B with its complicates edges.
